segments.he: הר' משה ברסלבר הנ"ל תלמיד מוהרנ"ת ז"ל הי' מתפלל מנחה בערב ראש השנה בהקלויז ופעם אחד כשהתחיל לומר קטורת וידבר ה' אל משה לאמור נפל חלשות והאריך זמן עד שהחיו אותו שאלו אותו מדוע נפל חלשות ענה ואמר שהתחיל וידבר ה' אל משה וכו' התבונן בעצמו שהשי"ת דיבר עם משה בשר ודם שבשר ודם יכול לזכך א"ע כ"כ שהשי"ת ידבר עמו והתעורר מזה כ"כ עד שנפל חלשות. איך האר זיך בא רעכינט אז השי"ת האט גרעט מיט משה. השי"ת האט גירעט מיט אבשר ודם וכו'...
segments.en:
Reb Mikheli of Tulchin, grandson of Moharan'as, said about communal prayer and its great virtue: it is accepted even if there are inferior members in the prayer — just as when one gives several coins together, even if there is an inferior coin among them it still passes. But if one gives only a single coin, it is examined carefully. So it is with communal prayer versus individual prayer. And Reb Mikheli lived in Tulchin and was very distinguished. He would study Torah publicly there, and after the prayer would stand with the other ardent members of our fellowship and speak with them of matters of the service of G-d. There were people there who were not of our fellowship and would speak idle words and news — disturbing our fellowship so they could not speak and study. They restrained themselves with all their strength from telling those people not to speak so loudly, so as not to come to a quarrel. Despite this they were so disturbed that they could not bear it — until one of our fellowship, Reb Shechin'a grandson of Moharan'as, said to Reb Mikheli: "I am going to tell them to stop disturbing us." Reb Mikheli answered: "Zog, zog!" [Say! Say!] And Reb Shechin'a thought he was being given permission to go tell them. Reb Mikheli completed his sentence: "Zog zikh — zog zikh!" [Tell yourself — say it to yourself!] When Reb Mikheli was in Eretz Yisroel and was at the grave of Rashbi and studied Zohar there, he said that he derived enormous pleasure from it — that he felt a completely different taste in the Zohar each time he studied it. But the taste he felt in the Zohar studied at the grave of Rashbi was wondrously far greater. He said about this: "It is good to drink from the tap itself." "S'iz gut tsi trunken fun tsapn." [At the root itself one feels a different taste.]

Reb Mikheli was remarkable in the matter of fulfilling the commandment of welcoming guests — especially in the matter of preparing the bed for the guest. For Moharan'as had seen in the Burnt Book the greatness of welcoming guests, and particularly the making of the guest's bed — that from every step one takes while preparing a guest's bed, an angel is created from each step. And their custom was to prepare the guest's bed better than their own — and Reb Mikheli would check by lying down on the bed himself to see if it was comfortable enough for him personally, and only then would give that bed to the guest. When Reb Mikheli traveled to Eretz Yisroel, the entire town of Tulchin accompanied him from one end of the city to the other.
